title: Emit route/model/tenant labels for Private dashboards + cardinality guardrails
author: Nadia Rahman
description:
Context: The Private observability minimum pack dashboards/alerts assume a consistent label schema across gateway + runtime metrics (tenant, route, model) so operators can slice latency/error/saturation by the dimensions they actually manage (route/policy, model version, tenant/workspace). Several of these labels were missing or inconsistent across components, and naïvely adding them risks exploding cardinality (e.g., raw HTTP path, arbitrary model strings). This PR adds the missing labels and introduces guardrails to keep series count bounded by configuration.

What’s in this PR: (1) Gateway: add route_id + tenant_id + model_id labels to request duration, request count, error counters, and streaming disconnect counters; route_id is derived from the configured Redwood route name (NOT raw URL path). (2) Runtime: add model_id + tenant_id labels to prefill/decode latency histograms, queue depth gauges, batch size histograms, and KV-cache hit/miss counters; ensure model_id is the canonical serving model identifier used by policy/routing (not the raw user-provided string). (3) Control/guardrails: introduce a label sanitizer + bounded label-set enforcement; unknown/unconfigured values are mapped to "unknown" and increment redwood_metrics_label_dropped_total{label=...,reason=...}. Route label emission is only enabled when a request is mapped to a named Redwood route; otherwise route_id="unknown". (4) Cardinality hard stops: add a per-process max distinct label value budget for route_id and model_id (defaults: route_id=250, model_id=500) with deterministic overflow bucket ("__overflow__"); overflow increments redwood_metrics_label_overflow_total{label=...}. (5) Docs/tests: add unit tests that validate required labels exist for the minimum-pack queries, and a stress test that simulates 5k unique paths to ensure we do not create 5k unique route_id series (we should cap/bucket as designed). Document the label contract and the new guardrail metrics.

Why this approach: Private customers frequently run multi-tenant and multi-route setups; without these labels, the baseline dashboards are either unusable or force customers into bespoke instrumentation. Using route_id from config keeps cardinality bounded and matches what operators reason about (routes/policies), while the overflow/dropped counters give SREs a way to detect misconfiguration early.

Rollout / compatibility: This does not rename existing metric names; it only adds labels to existing series. Prometheus will treat this as new time series, so expect a one-time increase in series count proportional to (#tenants * #routes * #models) but bounded by the configured budgets. Defaults are chosen to support the min-pack dashboards without blowing up small-to-medium installs. If a customer is extremely sensitive to series count, they can set REDWOOD_METRICS_LABEL_BUDGET_ROUTE_ID=0 and/or REDWOOD_METRICS_LABEL_BUDGET_MODEL_ID=0 to force all values into "__overflow__" (documented as “diagnostic only”).

Validation: Ran the min-pack dashboard queries against staging (private-vpc-ref) under synthetic load (300 rps, 20 concurrent streams, 8 models, 12 routes, 3 tenants). Verified new labels appear, dashboards render, and series count remains stable when hitting randomized URL paths. Also confirmed alerts relying on label joins (route/model) work as expected.

Follow-ups: ENG-2847 will add an automated installer validation step that checks for these labels’ presence in Prometheus after install; ENG-2860 will tune any burn-rate alerts that should aggregate over route/model by default.
commits: telemetry: add bounded label set helper + overflow/dropped counters
gateway: emit tenant_id/route_id/model_id on http + streaming metrics
runtime: plumb tenant_id/model_id into scheduler and kv-cache metrics
tests: add label-contract assertions + cardinality stress test
docs: update metrics contract + min-pack required label schema
conversation: Allison Grant (review): Adding labels is fine, but I’m worried about route cardinality. Please confirm we’re not using raw URL path anywhere and add a hard cap + a metric to detect overflow/drops. Also, document the expected label values for route_id/model_id so dashboards don’t depend on ambiguous strings.

Nadia Rahman (author): Agree. Updated implementation to strictly use configured route name (RouteSpec.name) and added label budgets + overflow bucket + redwood_metrics_label_overflow_total/redwood_metrics_label_dropped_total. Also added docs page with the label contract + examples of values.

Sean Gallagher (review): For SLO burn alerts in Private, we’ll want to aggregate by route_id but keep the option to drill down by model_id. Can we ensure the default queries don’t require high-card joins? Also, are we adding tenant_id everywhere consistently?

Nadia Rahman (author): Yup—tenant_id is now emitted on all gateway request metrics and the runtime latency/queue/kv metrics that back the min-pack dashboards. We’re not doing label-joins; the burn-rate alert templates can aggregate over route_id and ignore model_id unless a customer opts in. I added a test that asserts tenant_id exists on the required metric set.
Julian Moore (review): Runtime side: model_id source-of-truth should be the resolved serving model (post-routing), not request payload. Did we plumb the resolved id through the scheduler path?

Nadia Rahman (author): Yes—model_id now comes from the routing decision (ResolvedModel.id) and is passed into the scheduler metrics context. Added a regression test where the request specifies an alias but we emit the canonical resolved id.
Logan Wright (review): Minor: budgets default values—can we justify 250/500? Also please ensure budgets are configurable via env and config file (Private installs will want values.yaml hooks later).

Nadia Rahman (author): Added env overrides (REDWOOD_METRICS_LABEL_BUDGET_ROUTE_ID / _MODEL_ID) and documented sizing guidance. Defaults match our current largest Private reference topology with headroom; follow-up to add helm/installer wiring tracked in ENG-2852/ENG-2845 notes.
Allison Grant (final): Approved after caps + overflow metrics + docs landed. Please keep the contract page stable for the min-pack dashboards.
Merge: Squash merged by Nadia Rahman into main.
release_notes: Private observability: gateway/runtime metrics now include tenant_id/route_id/model_id labels required by the Private minimum observability pack dashboards; includes cardinality guardrails with overflow/dropped counters.
